misconceptions.description: Treating the module readiness checklist as a formality rather than a real self-check before moving on
misconceptions.trigger: learner marks every item complete without testing whether each skill works
misconceptions.feedback: Use the checklist to actually test each skill: open the artifact and confirm it meets the standard before checking the box.

misconceptions.description: Treating the module's skills as separate boxes rather than parts of one digital readiness practice
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies one skill without considering related ones in the same artifact
misconceptions.feedback: Skills combine: a resume artifact also needs truthful evidence, AI disclosure, accessibility, and privacy care at once.

misconceptions.description: Letting the AI studio decide readiness instead of judging your own evidence against the standard
misconceptions.trigger: learner asks the tool whether they are ready and accepts the verdict without checking artifacts
misconceptions.feedback: The studio supports your self-check; you confirm readiness by inspecting your own artifacts against each target.

misconceptions.description: Hiding weak areas to look finished instead of flagging gaps for targeted practice
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports full readiness while one skill is still shaky
misconceptions.feedback: Mark the gap honestly and request practice on that specific skill; a flagged weakness is more useful than a false all-clear.
